title: the stuck-session advisory
asserts: a session whose CLI writes the same tool call with identical arguments three times in a row is advised about, unsolicited and without anyone subscribing, and the advisory is exactly that - the session keeps running, keeps its pty and answers input afterwards, because the core notifies and never enforces.

steps.note: one ordinary turn first, so the file exists and the core can bind it
a core's first bind attempt lands on the spawn banner, before the file exists, so it backs off for BIND_RETRY; this outlasts that back-off
output is what makes a core read the transcript, so this is what gets the bind done and the opening turn read as backlog
three identical Bash calls with a tool result between each, which is the shortest run the detector advises on; no prompt is written, because a prompt would reset the chain
unsolicited: there is no subscribeStuck, for the same reason there is no subscribeActivity
the whole point: an advisory changes nothing. The session was not killed, not slept and not typed into, and it still answers
